---
title: "Fiscal Revenue, Trade Openness, and GDP in SAARC Countries (2000-2024)"
format: html
editor: visual
execute:
  echo: false
---

```{r}
#| message: false
library(WDI)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

saarc_countries <- c("AFG", "BGD", "BTN", "IND", "MDV", "NPL", "PAK", "LKA")

data <- WDI(
  country = saarc_countries,
  indicator = c(
    "NY.GDP.MKTP.CD",      # GDP
    "NE.TRD.GNFS.ZS",      # Trade openness
    "GC.REV.XGRT.GD.ZS"    # Revenue excluding grants
  ),
  start = 2000,
  end = 2024,
  extra = TRUE
)

data <- data |>
  rename(
    gdp = NY.GDP.MKTP.CD,
    trade = NE.TRD.GNFS.ZS,
    fiscal_revenue = GC.REV.XGRT.GD.ZS
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(gdp), !is.na(fiscal_revenue), !is.na(trade))

ggplot(data, aes(x = trade, y = gdp, color = country)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Trade Openness vs. GDP in SAARC Countries (2000-2024)",
    x = "Trade (% of GDP)",
    y = "GDP (current US$)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

**Summary**

This project compares fiscal revenue capacity, trade openness, and GDP across SAARC economies from 2000 to 2024 using World Bank World Development Indicators.

The analysis focuses on Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. Using the WDI API in R, the project retrieves and cleans regional macroeconomic data, then visualizes how trade openness relates to GDP across countries and years.

The current chart highlights a positive association between trade openness and GDP, especially for larger and more integrated economies in the region. Revenue excluding grants is included as a core fiscal-capacity variable to support broader comparisons of macroeconomic conditions across SAARC countries.
